Moving on, I'm confirming wound improvement always has a wound as participant, and wound length, morphology, and volume all plausibly inhere in the wound itself as qualities. Wound treatment doesn't always require a dressing as input, not all wounds are diabetic, WIfI stage concerns risk rather than being strictly about amputation, and microbial burden inheres in the wound as a quality.

For the remaining items, burn depth doesn't apply to every burn wound, diabetes doesn't universally have DFU as a part, gangrene's relation is miscategorized as subclass rather than correct part_of, necrotizing fasciitis involving subcutaneous tissue is uncertain since not every case may strictly include it as a part, and NF being part_of infection is really a subclass relationship rather than a true part_of.
